benchmark_name: Turbulent Flow in a Straight Square Duct

primary_reference.citation: Pirozzoli, S., Modesti, D., Orlandi, P., & Grasso, F. (2018). Turbulence and secondary motions in square duct flow. Journal of Fluid Mechanics, 840, 634-655.
primary_reference.secondary_reference: Vinuesa, R., Noorani, A., Lozano-Duran, A., El Khoury, G. K., Schlatter, P., Fischer, P. F., & Nagib, H. M. (2014). Aspect ratio effects in turbulent duct flows studied through direct numerical simulation. Journal of Turbulence, 15(10), 677-706.
primary_reference.database_repository: Sapienza University CFD Group DNS Database (http://newton.dma.uniroma1.it/square_duct/)

reynolds_number_definitions.bulk_reynolds_number_Re_b: Re_b = U_b * D_h / nu = U_b * (2*h) / nu
reynolds_number_definitions.naming_convention_note: Canonical dataset filenames square_duct_dns_Reb{Re_b}_Retau{Re_tau}.csv explicitly specify both bulk Reynolds number Re_b and friction Reynolds number Re_tau to eliminate ambiguity between bulk (Re_b) and half-width (Re_h) definitions. The legacy labels Re1500 and Re2200 reflected earlier arithmetic miscalculations in the initial repo draft.

canonical_dimensionless_space.description: Authoritative dimensionless representation used across all comparisons, scripts, and validation metrics

dns_reference_physical_scale.description: Direct numerical simulation database scaling (Pirozzoli et al. 2018)

openfoam_cfd_physical_scale.description: Dimensional laboratory duct scale simulated in OpenFOAM (verification_squareDuct case)

reference_vortex_cores_quadrant1.description: Normalized Q1 primary-vortex reference in quadrant y/h in [0, 1], z/h in [0, 1]. VERIFIED against the raw DNS export's own vorticity column (omx/(ub/h)) by scripts/validation/verify_dns_reference.py.

verification_provenance.legacy_peak_ratio_note: The legacy 2.03% target matches the raw Re_b=7000 (Re_tau=220) export peak exactly, not the Re_b=4410 plane (1.93% raw / 1.92% resampled); it was retained as a literature-style target. Tables now quote the raw-verified 1.93%.
verification_provenance.vorticity_discretization_check: Recomputed omega_x* from raw velocities agrees with the DNS-provided vorticity column to 0.43% of field max in the interior.

held_out_benchmark.case_name: Square Duct DNS at Re_tau = 220 (Re_b = 7000, Re_h = 3500)
held_out_benchmark.citation: Pirozzoli, S., Modesti, D., Orlandi, P., & Grasso, F. (2018). Turbulence and secondary motions in square duct flow. Journal of Fluid Mechanics, 840, 634-655.
held_out_benchmark.database_repository: Sapienza University CFD Group DNS Database (http://newton.dma.uniroma1.it/square_duct/)

training_data_caveats.description: Known provenance subtleties of the primary training dataset (square_duct_dns_Reb4410_Retau150.csv). Documented in detail in the README 'Honest Technical Discussion' section (limitation item 5).
training_data_caveats.gradient_provenance: grad_U_ij are second-order finite differences of the symmetry-mirrored, bilinearly resampled 65x65 cross-section (computed by scripts/convert_real_dns.py), not raw DNS gradients; near-wall gradient noise from the mirroring/resampling is baked in. All streamwise-derivative entries (grad_U_00, grad_U_10, grad_U_20) are identically zero, inherited from the streamwise-periodic reference DNS.
training_data_caveats.wall_boundary_ring: The 256 boundary points of the 65x65 grid have k clipped to 1e-7, giving targets a_ij = uu/(2k) - delta_ij/3 = -delta_ij/3 (trace -1) that are not valid anisotropy states for the trace-free tensor basis. These points are retained in the training loss: because every admissible network output is trace-free and Frobenius-orthogonal to I, the loss decomposes into the representable deviatoric part (dev(-I/3) = 0, so the network is trained toward a = 0 there) plus a constant zero-gradient offset from the incompatible trace part. The effect is confined to the invariant-space origin and has negligible bulk influence.
training_data_caveats.validation_split: The quadrant-1 spatial validation split (y > 0, z > 0) is reflection-degenerate: all five invariants are even in the rotation tensor, so the held-out quadrant shares identical invariant inputs with the training quadrants. The split legitimately tests the tensor-basis sign structure (the odd-in-w bases T2, T5, T7, T8, T10) but not independent-flow generalization.
